Create a graph data object

Source: R/graph-data.R
graph_data.Rd

graph_data() stores one homogeneous graph: node features, an edge index, optional edge features and weights, labels at node, edge and graph level, node and edge type codes, split masks and free metadata. Data are kept as ordinary R vectors and matrices; graph_tensors() turns them into torch tensors once, on the device you choose.

Usage

graph_data(
  x = NULL,
  edge_index = NULL,
  y = NULL,
  edge_attr = NULL,
  edge_weight = NULL,
  edge_y = NULL,
  graph_y = NULL,
  graph_attr = NULL,
  num_nodes = NULL,
  directed = TRUE,
  node_ids = NULL,
  node_type = NULL,
  edge_type = NULL,
  train_mask = NULL,
  val_mask = NULL,
  test_mask = NULL,
  metadata = list(),
  validate = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

Node features: numeric matrix with one row per node, a numeric vector (one feature), a numeric data frame, or NULL.

edge_index

Edges as a 2 by E matrix (row 1 source, row 2 target), an E by 2 matrix, or a data frame with columns from and to. Values are one based node indices. NULL means no edges.

y

Node labels: factor (classification), integer or numeric vector, or numeric matrix (multi target), one entry per node. Character labels are converted to a factor (as are character edge_y and graph_y).

edge_attr

Edge features, one row per input edge.

edge_weight

Positive or signed numeric edge weights, one per input edge.

edge_y

Edge labels, one per input edge.

graph_y

Graph label (scalar, factor of length one, or numeric vector).

graph_attr

Graph level features (numeric vector).

num_nodes

Number of nodes. Inferred from x, y, node_ids or the largest edge index when NULL.

directed

Whether edges are directed. See the edge direction section.

node_ids

External node identifiers, one per node. Default seq_len(num_nodes).

node_type, edge_type

Optional integer or factor type codes per node and per input edge. They are stored, not interpreted; typed learning uses hetero_graph_data().

train_mask, val_mask, test_mask

Logical node masks.

metadata

Named list of free metadata (source, version, notes).

validate

Run validate_graph() after construction.

Value

An object of class graph_data.

Indexing convention

Node indices are one based everywhere in the public API: node i is row i of x, and edge_index holds values in 1:num_nodes. R torch index operations (index_select, index_add, scatter_add, scatter_reduce) are also one based, so the stored indices are passed to torch unchanged. The only conversion to zero based indices happens in to_zero_based(), used when exporting to formats that require it.

Edge direction

edge_index is a 2 by E matrix; column j is a directed edge from edge_index[1, j] (source) to edge_index[2, j] (target). Messages flow from source to target.

With directed = FALSE, supply each undirected edge once. The stored graph holds both directions, (u, v) and (v, u), next to each other; a self loop is stored once. edge_pair maps every stored directed edge to the input edge it came from, and edge level values (edge_attr, edge_weight, edge_y, edge_type) are copied to both directions. If the input already contains reciprocal pairs, a warning is given, because those pairs would then be stored twice in each direction.

Examples

g <- graph_data(
  x = matrix(rnorm(8), 4, 2),
  edge_index = rbind(c(1, 2, 3), c(2, 3, 4)),
  y = factor(c("a", "b", "a", "b")),
  directed = FALSE
)
g
#> <graph_data> undirected graph: 4 nodes, 6 edges (3 undirected pairs)
#>   node features [4 x 2]
#>   node labels: factor with 2 levels
num_nodes(g)
#> [1] 4
num_edges(g)
#> [1] 6
num_edges(g, unique_pairs = TRUE)
#> [1] 3
